newsitem.title: USA: US CFTC gets court action against commodity pool.
newsitem.headline: US CFTC gets court action against commodity pool.

text.p: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) said on Tuesday that a Michigan District Court had entered a restraining order freezing the assets of Michigan commodity pool.

As well as freezing the assets of Daniel O'Shaughnessey, Glory Fund I, Inc, and Glory Fund LLC, the order also prohibits the destruction of the defendants books and records, the CFTC said in a statement.
The order stems from a November 21 CFTC complaint alleging that the defendents defrauded Glory Fund pool participants, and made false statements and false advertisements.
The complaint charged that since at least April, 1996, the defendants have violated the anti-fraud provisions of the Commodity Exchange Act.
The defendants allegedly cheated the and defrauded pool participants by misappropriating customer funds and by misrepresenting the performance of Glory Fund.
Later Tuesday, the court granted a preliminary injunction enjoining the defendants from violating federal commodity law and requiring the defendants to carry out an accounting.
The defendants consented to the injunction, but neither admitted nor denied the allegations, a CFTC spokesman said.
